title: Four early-extension drill options

context.format: Rapid vertical demonstration montage with on-screen cues and detailed creator post description
context.style: External constraints and sensations; four alternatives

coverage.transcript_kind: On-screen coaching text manually read from source frames; full creator description read separately
coverage.audio_transcription_note: ASR attempted and full output reviewed; repetitive output rejected as coaching evidence. No reliable spoken coaching transcript claimed.
coverage.visual_review_method: 15 overview and 38 detail frames across six portrait sheets, all inspected. Includes all four titles/cues, prop placement and quarter-second samples through shots. These are sampled frames, not continuous playback.
limitations: Four very short examples; no patient/student assessment.
Prop contact and exact impact not fully established by quarter-second samples.
Background simulator values lack a confirmed association and readable labels; not used as measurements.
ASR does not reliably represent the audio; coaching record uses visible text and creator description.

evidence.attribution: Jenny Kim: on-screen instructions and demonstrations; rationale/procedural detail from accompanying creator post text
evidence.summary: Opening title asks about early extension and offers four drills. Creator description defines the issue as hips moving toward the ball too early in downswing, reducing arm/club space. This is the stated target, not a diagnosis of the demonstrator.

frames.observation: Address view; no before-swing comparison or pelvis line.

limitations: No assessed student, initial fault capture or controlled before/after.

evidence.summary: Open-stance drill is labelled open stance plus rotate, with cue to create room for hips to turn. Creator text explains opening stance may help lower body rotate through instead of driving toward ball. One shot is demonstrated.
limitations: No assessed student, initial fault capture or controlled before/after.

evidence.attribution: Jenny Kim: on-screen instructions and demonstrations; rationale/procedural detail from accompanying creator post text
evidence.summary: Bucket drill places trail foot into/under a tipped basket opening. Title says keep trail leg back and avoid hitting bucket. Creator text specifies avoiding trail shin pushing into its top to discourage knee/hip driving toward ball. Demonstration goes to a normal finish.

evidence.summary: Alignment stick passes through an upright basket beside trail foot. Caption specifically says not to hit stick before impact. Timing of contact is the point; later contact is not categorically prohibited by the source.

cases.title: Try an open stance to make rotation through feel easier
cases.coaching_finding: Creator targets hips/trail side moving toward ball too early in downswing and reducing arm space. No individual golfer is assessed in this source.
cases.coach_reasoning: Creator explains an open stance can make lower-body rotation easier to feel, reducing intent to drive toward ball.

intervention.drill: Open stance as shown and make a controlled swing.
intervention.cue: Create room for the hips to turn.
intervention.scope: Source drill stance; not a universal permanent setup prescription.

applicability: Corresponding movement established in the golfer, rather than inferred from a single standing-up appearance.
Use one drill that gives a useful response; source says to try alternatives to find the best feel.
unknowns: Why the individual golfer moves toward the ball; club delivery, setup and physical-screen contributors not assessed.
Individual fit, precise prop placement and amount of movement.
Measured pelvis/pressure change, strike benefit, transfer or retention.
cases.observed_result: Instructor executes a demonstration shot. No baseline comparison, contact sensor or validated improvement is provided.

selection.coaching_focus: Retain space while rotating through delivery
selection.policy_origin: User one-focus constraint. Store four alternatives; select one, then reassess before switching.
selection.reassess: Proposed app check: compare actual pelvis/trail-side movement and strike without prop. For barrier drills, inspect contact timing rather than claim success from finish alone.

cross_source_links.relation: A diagnosis must precede matching an early-extension drill
cross_source_links.explanation: TPI rejected an initial early-extension hypothesis for Josh Allen after measurement. Kim’s tutorial supplies drill options only after a corresponding movement is established; a standing-up impression alone does not justify retrieval.

cross_source_links.relation: Do not change an effective motion solely to match an appearance
cross_source_links.explanation: Harrington withholds hip changes when motion works. Kim’s generic drills do not establish that another golfer needs a pelvis correction.

cross_source_links.relation: Barrier timing and normal trail-side movement must be kept distinct
cross_source_links.explanation: Harrington’s transition explanation permits trail-side movement and treats heel height as insufficient evidence. Kim’s stick cue is specifically before impact; do not turn it into a frozen trail leg or heel rule.

Allen’s initial right/left distribution adjustment concerns side-to-side setup. Kim’s toe feedback concerns forward movement into the trail forefoot during delivery. Do not conflate the two into a single pressure percentage.

within_source_distinctions.relationship: Four alternatives for one stated target, not a four-drill prescription. Open stance changes setup; bucket/stick provide contact feedback; ball supplies a pressure feel. Selection depends on individual response.

annotation_opportunities: Label all four drills as alternatives and expose only the chosen task.
Pair a confirmed impact event with barrier-contact timing if later available.
Distinguish prop-contact observation from inferred hip position and measured pressure.
Do not annotate every elevated trail heel as failure; all demonstrations allow a finish.
excluded_material: Claim that any demonstrator has early extension at baseline.
A prescription to stay down, freeze trail foot or keep weight right through impact.
Automated pressure readings from a ball under toes.
Background simulator numbers as proof of before/after improvement.

independent_validation.reason: Generic drill montage with creator rationale; no diagnostic assessment or validated result.
